en: Jose Rizal was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan, now known as Rizal Park in Manila.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines consists of one Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices.
The Philippine eagle, locally known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the official national bird.
Jasminum sambac, locally called sampaguita, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a distinctive two-step forward dance ritual.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato are famous for weaving t'nalak cloth from abaca fibers.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system where specific characters represent syllables rather than single letters.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to provide affordable healthcare for premature babies.
Juan Luna painted the Spoliarium, which won the first gold medal at the Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts.
The South Sea pearl, scientifically known as Pinctada maxima, is the official national gem of the Philippines.
